newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Second Thai deal on ice.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Second Thai deal on ice.

text.p: Thailand's economic and rating woes are depressing appetite for Thai debt securities, with yet another deal being put on ice until conditions improve.
Siam Commercial Public Bank Co Ltd Yankee's planned Yankee bond with 144a shelf registration, is on hold.
A banker close to the deal said spreads for Thai deals had widened, and Siam Commercial would hold back from issuing.
"I guess they'll wait until market conditions for Thai issuers improve," he added.
However, another banker involved in the bank's global US$1.5 billion MTN programme said the programme was on course.
"We're just waiting for the right timing to come into the market (with an issue)," she said.
Other Thai issuers may be pondering whether to return to the offshore debt market after a wave of credit rating downgrades and continued concern over the Thai economy, bankers said.
Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand last week pulled a five-year floating-rate note (FRN) just four days into its launch after being downgraded.
Korea Exchange Bank issued a one-year US$200 million FRN in London overnight at par to float at 45 basis points over the three-month London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR).
ANZ has launched syndication for Jet Airways of India to part-finance two Boeing 737-400 aircraft.
The US$50.4 million facility is for the first major aircraft acquisition by a private Indian operator.
It carries a coupon of 150 basis points over LIBOR, with monthly instalments representing interest and principal culminating in a final balloon payment to effect ownership transfer after 35 months.
An arranger group has formed for COSCO (Hong Kong) Group Ltd's US$200 million revolving credit/term loan facility.
Eight banks have joined HSBC Investment Bank as arrangers for the deal, which pays a margin of 75 basis points over LIBOR.
Fees are 30 basis points for co-arrangers committing US$10 million or above, and 25 basis points for senior managers committing US$5 million to US$9 million.
PT Kawasan Industri Jababeka has mandated Nomura International Hong Kong and Peregrine Fixed Income to arrange a US$150 million floating-rate note issue, bankers said.
The three-year facility will be launched into general syndication via a special-purpose company, but no pricing details are yet available.
Chase Manhattan plans bond-style syndication for its HK$2.0 billion FRCD, which should be launched in London on Thursday.

Nothing has emerged on pricing on the deal which follows three other similar three-year FRCDs in recent weeks, of which the lowest was priced to float at 20 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate (HIBOR).
Standard Chartered's FRCd issue last week was issued at par to float at 20 basis points over one-month HIBOR.

Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corp's issue last month was issued at par to float at 22 basis points over one-month HIBOR. Bank of East Asia's FRCD issue, also in May, was issued at par to float at 30 basis points over three-month HIBOR.
